Every Ocean Animal That Survived a Mass Extinction

The nautilus has been circling the same dark reef slopes for over five hundred million years, and at this point it feels less like a survivor and more like a permanent fixture of the ocean itself. While countless other ocean lineages rose, dominated, and vanished, the nautilus just kept going, outlasting the Late Devonian extinction, the catastrophic End-Permian event, the End-Triassic wipeout, and the asteroid impact that ended the dinosaurs. Its secret is almost offensively simple: a chambered spiral shell that functions as a precision buoyancy device, filling individual chambers with gas or fluid to glide effortlessly up and down the water column, combined with a lifestyle built around scavenging dead and dying animals on deep reef slopes rather than hunting at the surface where extinction pressures tend to hit hardest.
